macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks closed lower as oil-price and inflation worries weighed on risk sentiment
items.summary: The three major U.S. stock indexes fell for a second straight day, with the Nasdaq down 0.6% and both the S&P 500 and Dow off about 0.3%, as traders focused on elevated oil prices, the Strait of Hormuz dispute, and incoming inflation data. Wall Street also watched a weaker real-economy backdrop after July existing-home sales fell and July jobs data showed a 23,000-job loss.

items.title: AP: S&P 500 slipped 0.4%, Dow down 145 points, Nasdaq down 0.8% amid oil volatility
items.summary: U.S. stocks drifted below record levels as crude oil swung higher on uncertainty over Middle East supply routes. The AP also reported the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.69% from 4.72%, while several earnings names moved sharply, including Aramark higher on better-than-expected results and Intel lower after announcing a $20 billion stock sale.

items.title: Markets turned cautious ahead of U.S. CPI as oil gains lifted rate-hike fears
items.summary: Barron’s reported that futures were pointing lower and that the oil rally was increasing concern about inflation and the Federal Reserve’s policy path ahead of Wednesday’s U.S. CPI release. The piece said the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz was keeping pressure on risk assets, including bitcoin.

items.title: July jobs report showed a 23,000-job loss, reinforcing slowdown concerns
items.summary: CNN Business highlighted that U.S. employers cut 23,000 jobs in July, far below forecasts for a 95,000 gain, after June’s figure was also revised lower. The report framed the data as evidence of growing caution in the economy amid higher oil prices and policy uncertainty.

items.title: Existing-home sales fell in July and markets priced in possible Fed and ECB moves
items.summary: Barchart reported that U.S. July existing-home sales declined 1.7% month over month to 4.06 million, close to expectations, adding to signs of cooling activity. The same report said markets were pricing a 48% chance of a 25-basis-point Fed hike at the next FOMC meeting and an 88% chance of a similar move by the ECB.

items.title: Major equity movers included Cardinal Health, Aramark, and Intel
items.summary: Among notable company developments, Cardinal Health rose after reporting stronger-than-expected spring-quarter profit, Aramark jumped on better-than-expected profit and revenue, and Intel fell after announcing plans to sell $20 billion of stock at $95 per share. These moves stood out in a session dominated by macro and energy-related concerns.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP fall as risk-off sentiment hits crypto markets
items.summary: Leading cryptocurrencies traded lower over the past 24 hours, with Bitcoin near the low-$63,000s, Ethereum slipping below $1,900, and XRP also declining. The market saw more than $190 million to $200 million in liquidations, mostly from leveraged long positions, as traders reduced risk amid geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Bitcoin remains range-bound as ETF inflows offset selling pressure
items.summary: Bitcoin stayed trapped in the roughly $62,000 to $66,000 range, with spot price around $63,500 after a small daily decline. CoinDesk said steady ETF demand is being offset by selling from miners and corporate holders, leaving the market stuck ahead of key U.S. inflation data.

items.title: Ethereum weakens as liquidations mount and ETH treasury activity continues
items.summary: Ethereum traded around $1,870 to $1,900 and saw tens of millions of dollars in liquidations over 24 hours, with long positions hit hardest. Separate market coverage said BitMine continued buying ETH while SharpLink reported large quarterly losses tied to the decline in ETH prices.

items.title: XRP and other major altcoins extend losses while Dogecoin holds up better
items.summary: XRP fell in the latest session, while Solana and Cardano also weakened in broader market selling. Dogecoin outperformed some peers with a modest gain in one market snapshot, even as overall crypto capitalization slipped.

items.title: Grayscale withdraws ETF filings for Cardano, Hedera and Polkadot
items.summary: Grayscale pulled registration applications for ETF products tied to Cardano, Hedera, and Polkadot, while other altcoin-related products remain under review. The move highlights how the ETF pipeline for non-Bitcoin assets remains active but uneven.

items.title: US crypto legislation stalls as the CLARITY Act misses Senate deadline
items.summary: The CLARITY Act did not reach a Senate floor vote before the chamber's August recess, leaving the U.S. regulatory framework for crypto markets unresolved. The delay is one of the most notable policy developments in the last day.

items.title: Russia's central bank reportedly authorizes official trading of Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT
items.summary: Russia's central bank reportedly added Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether to a list of cryptocurrencies that can be officially bought and sold on exchanges. If confirmed, the move would mark a significant step toward broader institutional acceptance of digital assets in Russia.

items.title: Binance adds five tokens to monitoring tag, raising delisting risk
items.summary: Binance placed Moonbeam, ICON, Moonriver, SuperRare, and Sophon on its monitoring tag, which can precede removal from the platform. The move is a notable exchange-level project development affecting several smaller crypto assets.

items.title: Bitcoin miner Riot stock jumps after Anthropic AI deal
items.summary: Riot's stock surged after the company announced a $9.1 billion Anthropic AI deal, drawing attention to the intersection of crypto infrastructure and AI-linked capital markets activity. The development did not directly move Bitcoin, but it was one of the more notable crypto-adjacent corporate stories.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT desktop app for Linux
items.summary: OpenAI has released a dedicated ChatGPT desktop application for Linux, expanding native access to its chatbot beyond Windows and macOS. The move is part of a broader push to make ChatGPT available across major desktop platforms.

items.title: Google’s Gemini app reaches 1 billion users
items.summary: Google says the Gemini app has reached 1 billion users, putting it on pace with ChatGPT’s reported growth. The milestone underscores intensifying competition in consumer AI assistants.

items.title: OpenAI expands Daybreak cybersecurity program with new cyber-trained model
items.summary: OpenAI is broadening its Daybreak AI cybersecurity defense program and rolling out a new model trained for cyber use cases. The announcement highlights rising demand for AI tools aimed at security research and defense.

items.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
items.summary: Anthropic plans to add watermarking support for text generated by its models, including older ones. The company says the feature is intended to help identify AI-generated content.

items.title: OpenAI suspends work on part of upcoming model Astra over cybersecurity concerns
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly paused work on certain aspects of its upcoming model Astra after internal concerns about its cybersecurity capabilities. The decision reflects increased caution around powerful models that could be misused.

items.title: Meta releases new open AI model for developers
items.summary: Meta has released a new AI model for developers with a permissive open-source license, signaling another attempt to strengthen its open-model strategy. The launch comes as the company continues to reposition its broader AI efforts.

items.title: DeepMind’s WeatherNext model improves hurricane forecasting
items.summary: DeepMind researchers reported a weather prediction breakthrough using the open-source WeatherNext model, which can make accurate forecasts with lower-resolution weather data. The result could improve the speed and efficiency of forecasting systems.

items.title: Spotify will label ‘AI Persona’ profiles and exclude their music from recommendations
items.summary: Spotify said it will start flagging AI-generated persona profiles and will not recommend their music. The policy targets synthetic artist identities that use photorealistic AI-generated imagery.

items.title: Nvidia teams up with major financial institutions to scale AI infrastructure financing
items.summary: Nvidia announced a plan with six major financial firms to help create financing platforms for AI infrastructure, aiming to unlock hundreds of billions of dollars in investment. The development reflects a broader industry trend toward massive capital formation around AI data centers and compute.
